### POST /sources/v1

`createSourceV1` — Create source

This creates a specific source with a full source JSON representation. Any passwords are submitted as plain-text and encrypted upon receipt.

- Scopes: idn:sources:manage
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN, SOURCE_ADMIN, SOURCE_SUBADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `provisionAsCsv` (query) — default False — If this parameter is `true`, it configures the source as a Delimited File (CSV) source. Setting this to `true` will automatically set the `type` of the source to `DelimitedFile`. You must use this…
- Body (application/json): source
- Returns 201: source

### GET /sources/v1/{id}

`getSourceV1` — Get source by id

Use this API to get a source by a specified ID in SailPoint Identity Security.

- Scopes: idn:sources:manage, idn:sources:read
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN, SOURCE_ADMIN, SOURCE_SUBADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — Source ID.
- Returns 200: source

### PUT /sources/v1/{id}

`putSourceV1` — Update source (full)

Use this API to update a source in SailPoint Identity Security, using a full object representation. This means that when you use this API, it completely replaces the existing source configuration. These fields are immutable, so they cannot be changed: * id * type * authoritative * connector * connectorClass * passwordPolicies Attempts to modify these fields will result in a 400 error.

- Scopes: idn:sources:manage
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN, SOURCE_ADMIN, SOURCE_SUBADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — Source ID.
- Body (application/json): source
- Returns 200: source

### PATCH /sources/v1/{id}

`updateSourceV1` — Update source (partial)

Use this API to partially update a source in SailPoint Identity Security, using a list of patch operations according to the [JSON Patch](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6902) standard. These fields are immutable, so they cannot be changed: * id * type * authoritative * created * modified * connector * connectorClass * passwordPolicies Attempts to modify these fields will result in a 400 error.

- Scopes: idn:sources:manage
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN, SOURCE_ADMIN, SOURCE_SUBADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — Source ID.
- Body (application/json-patch+json): array of jsonpatchoperation
- Returns 200: source

### DELETE /sources/v1/{id}

`deleteSourceV1` — Delete source by id

Use this API to delete a specific source in SailPoint Identity Security. The API removes all the accounts on the source first, and then it deletes the source. You can retrieve the actual task execution status with this method: GET `/task-status/{id}`

- Scopes: idn:sources:manage
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN, SOURCE_ADMIN, SOURCE_SUBADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — Source ID.
- Returns 202: object

### POST /sources/v1/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies

`createProvisioningPolicyV1` — Create provisioning policy

This API generates a create policy/template based on field value transforms. This API is intended for use when setting up JDBC Provisioning type sources, but it will also work on other source types. Transforms can be used in the provisioning policy to create a new attribute that you only need during provisioning. Refer to [Transforms in Provisioning Policies](https://developer.sailpoint.com/docs/extensibility/transforms/guides/transforms-in-provisioning-policies) for more information.

- Scopes: idn:provisioning-policy-source-admin-operations:manage, idn:provisioning-policy:manage
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `sourceId` (path, required) — The Source id
- Body (application/json): provisioningpolicydto
- Returns 201: provisioningpolicydto

### POST /sources/v1/{id}/remove-accounts

`deleteAccountsAsyncV1` — Remove all accounts in source

Use this endpoint to remove all accounts from the system without provisioning changes to the source. Accounts that are removed could be re-created during the next aggregation. This endpoint is good for: * Removing accounts that no longer exist on the source. * Removing accounts that won't be aggregated following updates to the source configuration. * Forcing accounts to be re-created following the next aggregation to re-run account processing, support testing, etc.

- Scopes: idn:accounts:manage
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — The source id
- Returns 202: taskresultdto

### POST /sources/v1/{id}/agents-delete

`deleteSourceAgentsV1` — Delete source AI agents — **EXPERIMENTAL (header `X-SailPoint-Experimental: true`)**

Use this API to delete all AI agents that were aggregated into the given datasets on a source. Deletion runs as an asynchronous task, and the response contains the task's initial status. This API returns `400` when the source has no connector instance, when `datasetIds` is missing or empty, or when a deletion or aggregation is already running for the source. When agentic identity governance is not enabled for the tenant, or AI agent deletion is not available, this API returns `404`.

- Scopes: idn:dataset:manage
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN, SOURCE_ADMIN, SOURCE_SUBADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `id` (path, required) — Source ID.
- Body (application/json): deletesourceagentsrequest
- Returns 202: sourceagentdeletiontaskstatus

### GET /sources/v1/{sourceId}/approval-config/machine-account-delete

`getMachineAccountDeletionApprovalConfigBySourceV1` — Machine Account Deletion Approval Config

Retrieves the machine account deletion approval configuration for a specific source. This endpoint returns details about the approval requirements, approvers, and comment settings that govern the deletion of machine accounts associated with the given source ID.

- Scopes: idn:source-config:read, idn:source-config:write
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN, SOURCE_ADMIN, SOURCE_SUBADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `sourceId` (path, required) — source id.

### PATCH /sources/v1/{sourceId}/approval-config/machine-account-delete

`updateMachineAccountDeletionApprovalConfigV1` — Machine Account Deletion Approval Config

Use this endpoint to update the machine account deletion approval configuration for a specific source. The update is performed using a JSON Patch payload, which allows partial modifications to the approval config. This operation is typically used to change approval requirements, approvers, or comments settings for machine account deletion. The endpoint expects the source ID as a path parameter and a valid JSON Patch array in the request body.

- Scopes: idn:source-config:read, idn:source-config:write
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN, SOURCE_ADMIN, SOURCE_SUBADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `sourceId` (path, required) — machine account source ID.
- Body (application/json-patch+json): array of jsonpatchoperation
- Returns 200: accountdeleteconfigdto

### GET /sources/v1/{sourceId}/approval-config/account-delete

`getAccountDeleteApprovalConfigV1` — Human Account Deletion Approval Config

The endpoint retrieves the approval configuration for deleting human accounts from a specified source. It returns details such as whether approval is required, who the approvers are, and any additional approval settings. This helps administrators understand and manage the approval workflow for human account deletions in their organization. The response is provided as an AccountDeleteConfigDto object.

- Scopes: idn:source-config:read, idn:source-config:write
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN, SOURCE_ADMIN, SOURCE_SUBADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `sourceId` (path, required) — The Source id
- Returns 200: accountdeleteconfigdto

### PATCH /sources/v1/{sourceId}/approval-config/account-delete

`updateAccountDeletionApprovalConfigV1` — Human Account Deletion Approval Config

Updates the approval configuration for deleting human accounts for a specific source, identified by source ID. This endpoint allows administrators to modify settings such as whether approval is required, who the approvers are, and other approval-related options. The update is performed using a JSON Patch payload, and the response returns the updated AccountDeleteConfigDto object reflecting the new approval workflow configuration.

- Scopes: idn:source-config:read, idn:source-config:write
- User levels: ORG_ADMIN, SOURCE_ADMIN, SOURCE_SUBADMIN
- Parameters:
  - `sourceId` (path, required) — Human account source ID.
- Body (application/json-patch+json): array of jsonpatchoperation
- Returns 200: accountdeleteconfigdto
